title: AI compute economics & model internals (agent)
summary: From the token cost of Claude Code sessions through AI compute supply and prices, open models, transformer internals, training and post-training, to the architectures that might follow.

concepts.title: Paying for tokens
concepts.summary: What a Claude Code session costs, how to track it, and why premium models get metered.

concepts.title: How do I track Claude Code token cost?
concepts.summary: Use ccusage, /cost or the status line; token counts are exact, only claude-carbon's CO2 estimate is lossy.

concepts.title: Claude Fable 5
concepts.summary: Anthropic's top model; from June 23, 2026 it needs usage credits ($10/$50 per M tokens) until capacity allows.

concepts.title: Price isn't cost to serve
concepts.summary: Per-token prices are business decisions: they hold flat, then drop in steps when a successor launches.

concepts.title: The compute squeeze
concepts.summary: Why AI capacity is scarce: demand compounding faster than chips, memory, power and grid gear can be added.

concepts.title: Compute demand
concepts.summary: How much AI compute the world wants; bending upward as reasoning and agents multiply compute per request.

concepts.title: Usage growth
concepts.summary: More people and apps using AI: Nvidia puts it at roughly 100× over two years.

concepts.title: Inference overtakes training
concepts.summary: Inference becomes the main data-center load around 2027 (JLL); it compounds with usage, so demand is stickier.

concepts.title: Available AI compute
concepts.summary: Serving capacity actually online, gated in turn by chips, HBM, power and electrical gear.

concepts.title: The bottleneck keeps moving
concepts.summary: Power-bound through early 2025, chip-bound by late 2025, transformer- and switchgear-bound by mid-2026.

concepts.title: AI accelerators
concepts.summary: GPUs and TPUs; Nvidia takes most of the spend, and Blackwell is sold out.

concepts.title: HBM memory
concepts.summary: Fast stacked memory beside the chip; sold out for 2026 and rising from ~8% to ~30% of AI spend.

concepts.title: Power & grid connections
concepts.summary: Energizing sites: 30–50% of planned 2026 data-center capacity is expected to slip to 2028.

concepts.title: Electrical gear
concepts.summary: High-voltage transformers and switchgear; lead times grew from 12–18 to 36–48 months, the newest chokepoint.

concepts.title: Data-center buildout
concepts.summary: Over $600B of 2026 cloud capex (~$450B for AI); delayed projects land in 2027–28.

concepts.title: Newer chip generations
concepts.summary: Each generation serves the same model cheaper, mostly through more memory bandwidth and HBM, not raw FLOPs.

concepts.title: Frontier model price
concepts.summary: What the newest, most capable models cost you per token, and whether you can get them at all.

concepts.title: Jevons paradox
concepts.summary: Cheaper tokens raise total token use, so efficiency gains get consumed instead of cutting spend.

concepts.title: Frontier stays pricey, old tiers collapse
concepts.summary: Scarce premium capacity gets priced up or rationed while each fixed capability bar keeps getting cheaper.

concepts.title: When will the squeeze ease?
concepts.summary: Probably 2027–28 as delayed capacity lands, and only if frontier demand growth slows; nobody really knows.

concepts.title: Why AI keeps getting cheaper
concepts.summary: What 'inference is getting cheaper' measures, how fast, and why parameter count stopped tracking capability.

concepts.title: Cost of a fixed capability
concepts.summary: What the cheapest model reaching a given benchmark bar costs: the number behind 'inference is getting cheaper'.

concepts.title: A given model gets 100× cheaper yearly
concepts.summary: The reader's first reading of Epoch's trend (t9). Wrong: frozen weights get cheaper only in steps.

concepts.title: Fixed capability, not fixed model
concepts.summary: Epoch's decline tracks smaller new models re-reaching old benchmark bars, not one shipped model getting cheaper.

concepts.title: Serving cost per token
concepts.summary: What it costs a provider to generate a token; set mostly by memory traffic, batching and hardware.

concepts.title: Harder bars should cheapen slower
concepts.summary: The reader's hypothesis (t11) that cheap models take longer to catch top benchmarks. The data shows the opposite.

concepts.title: Decline is fastest at the top
concepts.summary: Top GPQA bin fell 31×/yr, bottom 1.7×/yr: new bars have the most room for cheaper catch-up.

concepts.title: The rate depends on how you measure
concepts.summary: From ~3×/yr (algorithms alone) to 900×/yr (all models at frozen list prices): one trend, different methods.

concepts.title: Algorithmic efficiency
concepts.summary: Capability per unit of compute from better methods: about 3×/yr, in pre-training and in inference.

attributes.rate_method: Compute needed for the same pre-training performance (Epoch)

concepts.title: Incremental work drives the decline
concepts.summary: The smooth ~3×/yr curve is many small wins; breakthroughs like MoE reset the ceiling years earlier.

concepts.title: Frontier parameter count
concepts.summary: Total weights in the biggest models: rose 1000× by GPT-4, then shrank, and is mostly undisclosed.

concepts.title: Frontier models got smaller
concepts.summary: After GPT-4 (~1.8T), GPT-4o (~200B) and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (~400B) were ~10× smaller (Epoch estimates).

concepts.title: Chinchilla scaling
concepts.summary: 2022 finding that models were too big for their data; ~20 training tokens per parameter is compute-optimal.

concepts.title: Frontier training compute
concepts.summary: Compute spent training frontier models, growing ~5×/yr since 2020: the 'scale' behind two-thirds of gains.

concepts.title: Parameters decoupled from capability
concepts.summary: Since ~2023 capability rides on training compute, data, algorithms and test-time compute, not size.

concepts.title: Measured rates beat forecasts
concepts.summary: Trust measured rates (Epoch, academics) over dollar forecasts and timing calls from chipmakers and analysts.

concepts.title: Epoch AI
concepts.summary: Independent research group tracking compute, prices and model size; the chat's most-trusted source.

concepts.title: Inference price-trend paper
concepts.summary: 2025 arXiv study splitting price declines by capability level and removing list-price and hardware effects.

concepts.title: LessWrong inference-progress analysis
concepts.summary: Write-up on algorithmic progress in inference; treats open-weight prices as the cleanest signal.

concepts.title: Analyst shops
concepts.summary: SemiAnalysis, McKinsey, Bloomberg Intelligence: supply and spend figures re-reported everywhere; directional only.

concepts.title: JLL

concepts.title: Nvidia (Jensen Huang)

concepts.summary: SemiAnalysis: memory went from ~8% of hyperscaler AI spend (2023–24) to ~30% (2026).

concepts.title: How a transformer works
concepts.summary: The decoder-only transformer piece by piece, in DeepSeek-V3's published shape.

concepts.title: Next-token prediction
concepts.summary: LLMs generate one token at a time, each predicted from everything before it.

concepts.title: Decoder-only transformer
concepts.summary: The architecture under every frontier LLM: embed tokens, refine them through a layer stack, predict the next.

concepts.title: Tokenizer
concepts.summary: Chops text into tokens from a fixed vocabulary (129,280 in DeepSeek-V3) before the model sees it.

concepts.title: Embedding
concepts.summary: Turns each token into a vector of the model's hidden size (7,168 numbers in DeepSeek-V3).

concepts.title: Layer stack
concepts.summary: 61 layers in DeepSeek-V3 (3 dense, 58 MoE), each with its own weights, applied in sequence.

concepts.title: Residual stream
concepts.summary: The running 7,168-wide vector per token; each layer adds an adjustment rather than replacing it.

concepts.title: Transformer block
concepts.summary: One layer: attention (tokens mix) then a feed-forward network (per token), each with residual and norm.

concepts.title: Attention
concepts.summary: Where tokens exchange information: each token looks up relevant earlier tokens and pulls in their content.

concepts.title: Attention heads
concepts.summary: Parallel query-key-value lookups in every layer (128 in DeepSeek-V3), each learning a different relationship.

concepts.title: Query, key, value
concepts.summary: Query: what a token looks for. Key: what it advertises. Value: what it hands over if matched.

concepts.title: KV-cache
concepts.summary: Past tokens' keys and values kept per layer so they aren't recomputed: inference's biggest memory cost.

concepts.title: Positional encoding (RoPE)
concepts.summary: Rotates queries and keys by position so attention sees relative distance; DeepSeek-V3 trained it at 4K.

concepts.title: Attention kernel
concepts.summary: The GPU code that computes attention; its speed depends on traffic between HBM and on-chip SRAM.

concepts.title: Feed-forward network (FFN)
concepts.summary: Per-token expand-then-contract network (7,168 → 18,432 → 7,168 in dense layers); where MoE plugs in.

concepts.title: Router
concepts.summary: A single linear layer scoring every expert for each token; the top-k (8 in DeepSeek-V3) get it.

concepts.title: Routed experts
concepts.summary: 256 small FFNs per MoE layer in DeepSeek-V3, each 7,168 → 2,048 → 7,168.

concepts.title: Shared expert
concepts.summary: An always-on expert every token uses (one in DeepSeek-V3), so routed experts needn't relearn basics.

concepts.title: Output head
concepts.summary: Projects the final vector to vocabulary logits: the model's single next-token prediction.

concepts.title: Attention's quadratic cost
concepts.summary: Every token attends to every earlier one, so attention cost grows with sequence length squared.

concepts.title: Each layer predicts a token
concepts.summary: The reader's guess (t23) that layers each make a prediction and the guesses get blended.

concepts.title: Only the last layer predicts
concepts.summary: Layers form a refinement pipeline; intermediate outputs are representations, not guesses (the logit lens can peek).

concepts.title: Depth, width & expert count
concepts.summary: Architects trade layers against vector width and experts; big open models run about 30–80+ layers.

concepts.title: Making models cheaper to run
concepts.summary: The techniques that cut memory, compute and cost, and which part of the model each one changes.

concepts.title: Inference is memory-bound
concepts.summary: GPUs mostly wait on data moving from HBM, so most optimizations move less data, less often.

concepts.title: Architecture buys efficiency; RL buys quality
concepts.summary: Most architecture changes are quality-neutral cost cuts; 2025's quality jumps came from post-training RL.

concepts.title: Serving stack
concepts.summary: The software that runs a trained model for many users: batching, number precision and the decoding loop.

concepts.title: Request batching
concepts.summary: Running many users' requests through the model together to keep the accelerator busy.

concepts.title: Numeric precision
concepts.summary: Bits per weight and activation (BF16, FP8, INT4); DeepSeek-V3 ships natively in FP8.

concepts.title: Decoding loop
concepts.summary: Generating output one token per forward pass, strictly left to right.

concepts.title: Serving optimizations
concepts.summary: Tricks that make frozen weights cheaper to serve without retraining: why a deployed model gets cheaper.

concepts.title: FlashAttention
concepts.summary: Computes attention in SRAM-sized tiles in one fused pass, never writing the full score matrix to HBM.

concepts.title: PagedAttention
concepts.summary: Stores the KV-cache in small pages, like OS virtual memory, so no memory sits reserved but empty.

concepts.title: Prefix caching
concepts.summary: Computes a shared prompt prefix's KV-cache once and reuses it: why cached input is ~90% off.

concepts.title: KV-cache quantization
concepts.summary: Stores keys and values in 8 bits or fewer, halving cache memory; keys are more sensitive than values.

concepts.title: Weight quantization
concepts.summary: Runs weights at lower precision (FP8, INT8, INT4), often with negligible quality loss.

concepts.title: Continuous batching
concepts.summary: Swaps requests in and out of a running batch so the accelerator stays saturated.

concepts.title: Speculative decoding
concepts.summary: A small draft model proposes several tokens; the big model checks them all in one parallel pass.

concepts.title: Trained-in efficiency
concepts.summary: Efficiency built in at training time: shrinks the KV-cache or attention cost at the source.

concepts.title: Multi-query attention (MQA)
concepts.summary: All query heads share one key/value head, shrinking the cache ~N× but denting quality.

concepts.title: Grouped-query attention (GQA)
concepts.summary: Query heads share K/V heads in groups (e.g. 32 → 8): most of MQA's savings, little quality loss.

concepts.title: Multi-head latent attention (MLA)
concepts.summary: Caches a 512-wide latent instead of 16,384 K/V numbers per token-layer and rebuilds heads on the fly.

concepts.title: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)
concepts.summary: A cheap 'lightning indexer' picks relevant earlier tokens and attention runs only on them: O(L·k), not O(L²).

concepts.title: Linear attention
concepts.summary: Cheap attention in most layers, full attention in a few (Kimi Linear: 1 in 4), for higher throughput.

concepts.title: Position interpolation
concepts.summary: Extends context by squeezing all positions into the trained range; blurs nearby-token distinctions.

concepts.title: YaRN
concepts.summary: Frequency-aware context extension: stretches long-range RoPE frequencies, keeps local ones (4K → 160K in DeepSeek-V3).

concepts.title: NoPE
concepts.summary: Drops positional encoding in some layers and relies on the causal mask for order (SmolLM3, Kimi Linear).

concepts.title: Multi-token prediction (MTP)
concepts.summary: Extra heads trained to predict several tokens ahead; in DeepSeek-V3 they double as speculative drafts.

concepts.title: KV-cache sharing across layers
concepts.summary: Adjacent layers reuse one key/value cache instead of each storing its own.

concepts.title: Cross-layer parameter sharing
concepts.summary: Layers reuse the same weights (ALBERT): far fewer parameters, but just as much compute.

concepts.title: Layer pruning
concepts.summary: Removing near-redundant middle and late layers from a trained model, with modest quality loss.

concepts.title: Mixture of experts (MoE)
concepts.summary: Replaces each FFN with many experts and a router: the capacity of all parameters, the cost of a few.

concepts.title: Total vs active parameters
concepts.summary: MoE splits size in two: total (memory, capacity) vs active per token (compute, cost), e.g. 671B vs 37B.

concepts.title: Experts aren't topic specialists
concepts.summary: Routing changes every token at every layer; experts learn low-level patterns, not 'chemistry' or 'law'.

concepts.title: Load balancing
concepts.summary: An auxiliary loss and capacity caps stop the router overusing a few experts and leaving the rest dead.

concepts.title: Aux-loss-free balancing
concepts.summary: DeepSeek's per-expert bias terms balance load without an auxiliary loss's quality penalty.

concepts.title: Fine-grained experts
concepts.summary: Many small experts (DeepSeek: 256, each 2,048 wide) instead of a few large ones (Llama 4: 8,192 wide).

concepts.title: Dropping the shared expert
concepts.summary: Qwen3 has no always-on expert while DeepSeek, Kimi K2 and GLM-4.5 keep one: still unsettled.

concepts.title: Expert parallelism
concepts.summary: Spreading experts across GPUs and shipping tokens to them; the traffic shapes designs (GLM-5's 80 layers).

concepts.title: History of MoE
concepts.summary: 1991 idea (Jacobs, Hinton et al.), 2017 sparse gating (Shazeer), GShard 2020, Switch 2021, open default by 2025.

concepts.title: The open models
concepts.summary: The open-weight flagships' shapes and signature ideas, from DeepSeek-V3 to GLM-5.2.

concepts.title: DeepSeek-V3
concepts.summary: DeepSeek's 671B MoE (37B active): the best-documented open model, with its full config public.

attributes.standout: MLA, aux-loss-free balancing, multi-token prediction, native FP8

concepts.title: DeepSeek-V3.2
concepts.summary: V3.1-Terminus plus DSA, nothing else architectural; scaled RL gave self-reported GPT-5-level results; API prices fell 50%+.

concepts.title: DeepSeek-R1
concepts.summary: DeepSeek's reasoning model: RLVR alone brought out long chains of thought and self-reflection (the 'aha moment').

concepts.title: Llama 4 Maverick
concepts.summary: Meta's first MoE: 400B total, 17B active, 1M context, ~22T training tokens; the conservative reference design.

attributes.standout: Alternates MoE and dense layers; sibling Scout: 109B, 10M context

concepts.title: Qwen3
concepts.summary: The Qwen team's open family, rated top of its size classes; uses GQA and drops the shared expert.

attributes.standout: Dropped the shared expert; tops its size classes

concepts.title: Kimi K2
concepts.summary: Moonshot AI's 1T-parameter MoE with 32B active and 384 experts; borrows MLA from DeepSeek.

concepts.title: GLM-5
concepts.summary: Zhipu's 744B MoE (40B active), MIT-licensed; its novelty is the slime async-RL pipeline, not the backbone.

attributes.standout: Imported DSA; 80 layers to cut expert-parallel traffic; slime async RL; 28.5T tokens; reportedly trained on Huawei Ascend

concepts.title: GLM-5.2
concepts.summary: June 2026 update: 1M-token context and High/Max reasoning modes; benchmark claims unverified, no tech report yet.

concepts.title: Open weights, not open data
concepts.summary: Open models share weights and inference code, some training code (DeepSeek most), never the data.

concepts.title: Techniques spread within months
concepts.summary: DSA went from DeepSeek-V3.2 into GLM-5's backbone within months; MLA reached Kimi K2.

concepts.title: Training & post-training
concepts.summary: How models are trained: pre-training on data, then post-training (SFT, preferences, RL) that shapes behaviour.

concepts.title: Pre-training
concepts.summary: Next-token prediction over trillions of tokens: the expensive phase that builds knowledge and capability.

concepts.title: Base model
concepts.summary: What pre-training produces: a raw next-token predictor with latent skills but no urge to help.

concepts.title: Post-training
concepts.summary: Everything after pre-training that turns a base model into an assistant; cheap, but shapes most behaviour.

concepts.title: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
concepts.summary: Training on curated prompt → ideal-response pairs; teaches the assistant format, but only imitates.

concepts.title: Preference learning
concepts.summary: Collecting 'A is better than B' judgments, usually to train a reward model that scores responses.

concepts.title: RL fine-tuning
concepts.summary: The model generates, a reward scores it, and training favours high scorers, so it can exceed its demonstrations.

concepts.title: RLHF
concepts.summary: RL against a reward model of human preferences: good for tone and helpfulness, but a gameable proxy.

concepts.title: DPO
concepts.summary: Optimizes directly on preference pairs, skipping the separate reward model; popular in open models.

concepts.title: RLVR
concepts.summary: RL where a checker (tests, known answers) gives the reward: now the main way to train reasoning.

concepts.title: GRPO
concepts.summary: Drops PPO's critic network and scores each attempt against its group's average, making reasoning RL affordable.

concepts.title: RLVR failure modes
concepts.summary: Length bias, exploration collapse and reward hacking, each patched by a GRPO variant (DAPO, GSPO, …).

concepts.title: RLVR sharpens, may not expand
concepts.summary: One study: RLVR makes right answers likelier but solves fewer distinct problems than the base model; contested.

concepts.title: Rewards beyond math and code
concepts.summary: The open problem: learned verifiers, rubrics and step-level rewards to bring RLVR to fuzzy domains.

concepts.title: Agentic RL
concepts.summary: RL for tool use and long multi-step tasks: the current frontier (GLM-5's slime pipeline).

concepts.title: Test-time compute
concepts.summary: Capability from thinking longer at inference; multiplies compute per request (~10,000× in two years, per Nvidia).

concepts.title: Distillation
concepts.summary: Training a smaller student on a stronger model's outputs; cuts serving cost and spreads capabilities.

concepts.title: Distillation built open chat models
concepts.summary: 2023–24 open models learned to chat from GPT outputs: Alpaca (52K instructions), Open Orca, ShareGPT.

concepts.title: Distillation drives open reasoning gains
concepts.summary: The assistant's own line (t36b), retracted in t44 as overreach: no data pins that share down.

concepts.title: R1's reasoning came from RL
concepts.summary: In the best-documented case RL created the reasoning; distillation then spread it to smaller models.

concepts.title: Full fine-tuning
concepts.summary: Updating every weight at a low learning rate; frontier labs use it for RL, and it risks catastrophic forgetting.

concepts.title: LoRA
concepts.summary: Freezes the model and trains small low-rank adapters (e.g. 7,168×16): cheap, swappable, no forgetting.

concepts.title: Specialists or one generalist?
concepts.summary: Both kinds of transfer are real and uneven, so labs blend: data mixing, staged training, merging.

concepts.title: Negative transfer
concepts.summary: Training on one task hurts another; in one study specialists beat the all-data model on 5 of 7 tasks.

concepts.title: Positive transfer
concepts.summary: Training on one task helps another (math improves code); data-rich tasks carry data-poor ones.

concepts.title: Transfer is asymmetric
concepts.summary: Code and math are safe donors; factuality and fairness help themselves but harm others (one 2025 study).

concepts.title: Model merging
concepts.summary: Train specialists on shared plus domain data, then average their weights into one model.

concepts.title: Training data
concepts.summary: What goes into pre- and post-training corpora, and how much of the work building them is.

concepts.title: Open-data corpora
concepts.summary: Fully open pre-training sets built on filtered Common Crawl plus code, papers, books and Wikipedia.

concepts.title: Corpus refinement
concepts.summary: Extract clean text, deduplicate by document and paragraph, then keep the top ~10% by a quality classifier.

concepts.title: DCLM
concepts.summary: Benchmark fixing the model and varying only the data; its filtered set beat the open-data best at half the compute.

concepts.title: Data is the main lever
concepts.summary: Curation buys what would otherwise take double the compute; data work likely rivals architecture work.

concepts.title: Post-training data
concepts.summary: Demonstrations and preference pairs from annotators, real users and synthetic personas, cleaned of benchmark leaks.

concepts.title: Tülu 3
concepts.summary: Ai2's fully open post-training recipe; its new synthetic SFT answers came from GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

concepts.title: LLM-as-a-judge
concepts.summary: Models, not humans, now rank most preference pairs; humans stay where judgment is hardest.

concepts.title: Beyond the transformer
concepts.summary: Attempts to replace parts of the recipe: state-space models, hybrids, bytes, diffusion and latent reasoning.

concepts.title: Can simpler wiring match transformers?
concepts.summary: At up to 1.3B parameters, yes (Mamba); at frontier scale, hybrids that keep some attention win.

concepts.title: Attention-free models
concepts.summary: Replace attention with a fixed-size recurrent state: constant memory per token, no growing KV-cache.

concepts.title: Mamba
concepts.summary: Selective state-space model with one repeated block, no attention or MLP; matched transformers up to 1.3B.

concepts.title: A fixed state forgets details
concepts.summary: A fixed-size state is a lossy summary, so SSMs are weaker at precise recall, reasoning and code.

concepts.title: Mamba–attention hybrids
concepts.summary: Mostly Mamba layers with ~1 attention layer per 5–7: comparable quality, more throughput, less memory.

concepts.title: Jamba
concepts.summary: AI21's hybrid, up to 398B parameters with 7 of 8 blocks Mamba; matched Mixtral and Llama-2 70B.

concepts.title: Nemotron-H
concepts.summary: NVIDIA's 8B and 56B hybrids that swapped most attention for Mamba and were fully post-trained.

concepts.title: Granite 4.0
concepts.summary: IBM's late-2025 hybrid; its Small model beat every open model on IFEval but one 12× its size.

concepts.title: Byte Latent Transformer (BLT)
concepts.summary: Meta's tokenizer-free model: groups raw bytes into entropy-sized patches; matched Llama 3 up to 8B.

concepts.title: Diffusion language models
concepts.summary: Generate a whole block in parallel by iterative denoising; shipped by Inception and Google at 5–10× speed.

concepts.title: Block diffusion
concepts.summary: Autoregressive across ~32-token blocks, diffusion within each: the standard production design.

concepts.title: Mercury
concepts.summary: Inception Labs' dLLMs: Mercury Coder (Feb 2025) was first to market; Mercury 2 reasons at ~1,000 tokens/s.

concepts.title: Gemini Diffusion
concepts.summary: Google's dLLM (May 2025): ~1,479 tokens/s, with coding scores matching its autoregressive sibling.

concepts.title: Diffusion makes reasoning cheaper
concepts.summary: Long chains of thought, slow token by token, can be filled in parallel; vendor-reported, and contested.
